A_general.open_code_note: No official repository was identified in the prepared repository list or local code folder. The public Glama repositories describe community servers and are not evidence of the deployed Strava endpoint.
A_general.release_status: Launched June 1, 2026; official sources describe it as launched and available to subscribers.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Access is included with an active Strava subscription, Strava + Runna bundle, Family Plan, Student Plan, or listed Military, Educator, and Medical Discount subscriptions. Trial subscriptions do not grant access until they convert to paid subscriptions. No separate MCP charge is listed.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Strava offers free access and paid subscriptions. The pricing page lists €10.99/month or €74.99/year in the listed European countries, Family Plan €129.99/year, and Strava + Runna Plan €149.99/year.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP access is an included subscriber feature. The connector article says requests are limited per minute and per day but does not publish the quotas.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Subscriber access required; trials excluded until paid conversion. Official launch materials say rollout is global. The official help center describes Claude as the launch client and says other AI clients may be supported in the future.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Strava controls subscriber eligibility, endpoint access, scopes, and request limits; the user authorizes and can revoke access in Strava settings.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The connector exposes read-only access to personal Strava data. The official help center describes supported subject areas but does not publish tool names or schemas. Anthropic's connector listing names eight tools.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool result structure and error format are NOT FOUND in available official materials.

Official materials do not describe MCP prompts.
No MCP logging behavior or user-visible logging facility is documented for the connector.
Official materials do not describe MCP sampling.
Official materials do not describe MCP roots.

The protected-resource document identifies the resource as https://mcp.strava.com/mcp, authorization server https://www.strava.com/mcp-issuer, and header bearer tokens. The issuer metadata advertises authorization_code and refresh_token grants and a registration endpoint. The provided metadata does not state PKCE requirements, token authentication methods, or token lifetime. The endpoint POST evidence supplied for this study returned HTTP 403 HTML without a WWW-Authenticate header; the separate connection-test evidence says HTTP 401.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration endpoint present at https://www.strava.com/oauth/mcp/register_client; authorization_code and refresh_token grants; response type code; bearer token via header; scopes_supported: read, read_all, activity:read, activity:read_all, profile:read_all. PKCE, client authentication methods and token lifetime NOT FOUND. Revocation endpoint: https://www.strava.com/oauth/mcp/revoke.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Official materials do not describe server-initiated elicitation or a confirmation flow.
Official materials do not describe MCP tasks or durable task execution.

The connector is connected and disconnected through Strava, Claude, or Claude Code settings. The help center describes account authorization and revocation, but does not document tool filters, URL parameters, or configuration headers.
No official connector error schema or MCP error-reporting capability is documented.
Subscription is an access requirement, but no MCP subscription capability is documented.
Official materials do not describe MCP progress notifications.
Official materials do not describe MCP request cancellation.

The official help center describes a remote connector that gives conversational access to live account data, including subscription analytics, training history, fitness trends, readiness, goal planning, cross-sport training, and gear.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Officially described as read-only; the help center says it cannot upload or edit activities. Native annotations are not published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation or approval flow is documented; no writes are described. 3. OAuth metadata lists read, read_all, activity:read, activity:read_all, profile:read_all scopes. Account authorization and revocation are described; whether Strava account roles or privacy settings are inherited is not specified. DCR and revocation endpoints are published; client allowlists, redirect approval, PKCE, token lifetime and admin switches are NOT FOUND. 4. No read-only mode parameter, toolset filter, query-free mode, or alternate official region endpoint is documented. 5. Official statements say access is read-only and scoped to the connected account. Specific field masking or PII exclusions are NOT FOUND. 6. The help center says per-minute and per-day request limits apply, without publishing values. Bulk caps, time-range caps, truncation and per-call costs are NOT FOUND. 7. Validation and parameter correction are NOT FOUND. 8. Strava's API Policy says it may monitor and collect Usage Data; connector-specific logging and opt-out details are NOT FOUND. 9. The eight listed tool names contain no feedback, rating, report, survey, or suggestion tool. No connector upsell result is documented. 10. No initialize instructions or server-delivered skill is published. 11. No persistent agent memory behavior is documented. 12. One hosted endpoint is documented; no hierarchical or proxied server structure is described. 13. No raw API request, SQL, script, or general execution tool appears in the published eight-name listing.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: Available evidence describes a single hosted endpoint and a flat connector tool listing; no nested servers or configurable toolsets are documented.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official vendor tool-name list was found in Strava's help article, FAQ, press release, official domain pages, endpoint pages, or public vendor repository search; the official help article describes capabilities but gives no tool count. Anthropic's Claude connector directory lists 8 names and labels the connector “Anthropic verified”; these are third-party-listed names, not an official Strava tool reference. No catalogue-only tools were added from Glama because its pages describe distinct community servers; Composio's page is an API toolkit rather than the native endpoint. mcp.so identifies the endpoint but detects no tools. Smithery does not provide a tool list in the collected page.

actions.description: Retrieve time-series data streams for an activity.
Retrieve information about a Strava club.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code of the deployed server or verbatim official tool definitions and initialize instructions were available to serialize.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The official help center says the MCP cannot upload or edit activities, actions available through Strava's app/site or API but excluded from this read-only connector. Users can export their own data through Strava's Bulk Data Export Tool. Sources: https://support.strava.com/en-us/articles/15401531-strava-mcp-connector ; https://m.strava.com/legal/api_policy

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The support article gives example questions about training history, fitness trends, readiness, goals, cross-sport training, and gear. No behavioural rule for the AI is documented as a server instruction.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Strava states: “The MCP is read-only. It cannot upload or edit activities.” It also says access is “scoped to your account” and “revocable at any time in Strava settings.” The API Policy says Strava may monitor and collect Usage Data; connector-specific monitoring details are not stated.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Strava describes live access to account data rather than a static export and says answers can differ from Strava app insights because AI clients process information differently.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Read-only behavior and account-scoped, revocable access are stated for the connector, but public implementation evidence is unavailable. Per-minute and per-day limits are stated without values. General API Policy monitoring language does not establish connector-specific logging details.

contradictions: The supplied connection-test evidence states HTTP 401, while the pre-fetched endpoint POST response supplied for this analysis is HTTP 403 Forbidden HTML and includes no WWW-Authenticate header. The protected-resource OAuth metadata is available at the endpoint origin.

Anthropic's third-party connector listing names eight tools, while Strava's official help materials do not publish names or a tool total. The names therefore cannot be cross-checked against an official tool list.
observations_for_research: The Strava API Policy calls Strava MCP the sole authorized first-party agent-mediated interface and limits its use to subscribers' personal use of their own data.
OAuth metadata advertises both broad read scopes and activity/profile-specific read scopes; documentation characterizes the connector as account-scoped and read-only.
notes: Checked links.json, pages/ including the official English help article and its extracted page script, FAQ, press release, pricing, API Policy, endpoint-origin pages, and collected catalogues. The prepared code folder contains no repository checkout; the GitHub commit list is empty. Claude's connector directory is third-party evidence for the tool names. Glama's Strava listings describe separate community servers and were excluded from endpoint actions. Composio's Strava page describes its own API toolkit. No official tool schemas, initialize instructions, protocol version, token lifetime, PKCE details, quota values, or connector-specific logging behavior were found.
